title: Janelia Atalanta Series Plasmid Cloning
author: David Stern
materials: Using sequence editing software cut and paste the 20 gRNA target recognition sequence and the left and right homology arms into the provided template sequences. IMPORTANT: The gRNA sequence should be the 20 bp target sequence, excluding the NGG PAM sequence. The experiment will fail if you include the NGG sequence. Double check to make sure you have inserted all the sequences in the correct orientation! For example, the gRNA should be in forward direction relative to target gRNA sequence (not necessarily in forward direction relative to the genomic target). In addition, the orientation of the homology arms in the synthesized attL fragments should match their orientation in the genome. Some software "flips" sequences extracted from the genome, so double check that he orientation is as expected.

Add the reagents in the order specified. DO NOT make a master mix of the double Gateway plasmid and the Clonase. Doing so will result in dramatically reduced cloning efficiency, often resulting in zero positive colonies. Let mixture site on ice for 30 min
0.125 uL Proteinase-K (from Clonase kit) Incubate 37°C 20 min in thermocycler with heated lid. We have observed that this step is not critical for successful cloning.

Using sequence editing software cut and paste the 20 gRNA target recognition sequence and the left and right homology arms into the provided template sequences. IMPORTANT: The gRNA sequence should be the 20 bp target sequence, excluding the NGG PAM sequence. The experiment will fail if you include the NGG sequence. Double check to make sure you have inserted all the sequences in the correct orientation! For example, the gRNA should be in forward direction relative to target gRNA sequence (not necessarily in forward direction relative to the genomic target). In addition, the orientation of the homology arms in the synthesized attL fragments should match their orientation in the genome. Some software "flips" sequences extracted from the genome, so double check that he orientation is as expected.

Perform Gateway cloning reaction. Add reagents in this order: 1 uL 100 ng/uL double Gateway plasmid 0.5 uL 50 ng/uL attL3-tRNA-gRNA-LeftHomologyArm-attL4 synthesized dsDNA 0.5 uL 50 ng/uL attL5-RightHomologyArm-attL6 synthesized dsDNA 0.25 uL LR Clonase II enzyme mix (Thermo Fisher) Incubate at least 2 hours at 25°C in thermocycler with heated lid. Important Note 1: Add the reagents in the order specified. DO NOT make a master mix of the double Gateway plasmid and the Clonase. Doing so will result in dramatically reduced cloning efficiency, often resulting in zero positive colonies. Apparently the Clonase needs to encounter the attL and attR sites together for efficient cloning. Note 2: The published protocol specifies 1 hour incubation, but the double Gateway reaction is less efficient than single Gateway cloning and I have found that a longer incubation improves cloning efficiency. I often leave these reactions overnight. Note 3: Thermo Fisher sells a Gateway Clonase that is advertised to be optimized for cloning multiple attL fragments into a single plasmid (as we are doing here). The enzyme is twice as expensive as the normal Clonase. So far, I have always had success with the original Clonase, so I haven't tried the optimized enzyme. Note 4: Some users have reported that the mass of DNA provided by Twist can be off by as much as a factor of 3. They have found that measuring the actual concentration of the dissolved DNA and normalizing to 50 ng/uL substantially reduces the variability in their cloning efficiency.

steps.title: Prepare pJAT Plasmid Stock
steps.instruction: Transform pJAT into ccdB Survival cells and propagate the plasmid.

substeps.instruction: Transform pJAT into ccdB Survival cells following standard protocol.
Plate cells on LB + Ampicillin (100 ug/mL) and grow at 37°C for at least 15 hours.
Pick one colony and grow in 3 mL LB with antibiotics (Ampicillin 100 ug/mL, Chloramphenicol 25 ug/mL, or Spectinomycin 50 ug/mL) overnight shaking at 225 RPM at 37°C.
Perform standard mini-prep the next day.

steps.title: Design gRNA and Homology Arms
steps.instruction: Identify target sites and design the homology arms for synthesis.

substeps.instruction: Use computational tools (e.g., flyrnai.org/crispr3/web) to identify a high efficiency gRNA target site.
Identify homology arms (between 250 bp and 1000 bp) that flank the expected Cas9 cut site, ideally destroying the gRNA target site upon integration.

steps.title: Synthesize attL Homology Arm Pieces
steps.instruction: Synthesize the left and right homology arm pieces including attL sites.

substeps.instruction: Synthesize arms with attL sites (e.g., via Twist), leaving adaptor sequences on.
If synthesis fails due to GC content variance, edit AT or GC rich regions with a few mutations to balance content, but do not edit attL sites or the tRNA-gRNA-tRNA region.

steps.title: Assemble attL Components
steps.instruction: Configure the sequence for the final assembly.

substeps.instruction: Ensure attL3/attL4 and attL5/attL6 are oriented inwards toward each other.
Replace the indicated gRNA sequence with the target 20 bp gRNA.
Concatenate the sequences as: attL3 + Homology Arm Left + attL4 and attL5 + Homology Arm Right + attL6.
If using an Atalanta plasmid for two gRNAs, use the attL6 arm containing the tRNA-gRNA-tRNA array.
Prepare agar solution: 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 15 g agar, and 750 mL water; autoclave.
Prepare sucrose solution: 100 g sucrose and 250 mL water; filter sterilize using a 0.2 micron filter.
Mix the sucrose solution into the cooled (but not set) agar.
Add Spectinomycin to a final concentration of 100 ug/mL and pour plates.

steps.title: Transform Gateway Reaction
steps.instruction: Transform the Gateway reaction into competent cells.

substeps.instruction: Gently mix the entire ~2.25 uL reaction with 50 uL of DH5alpha (or equivalent, such as Zymo Mix & Go!) competent cells.
Rapidly move the tube to a 42°C block or water bath for 30 sec without shaking.
Move tube to ice for a few minutes.
Add 150 uL SOC.
Tape tube on its side to a 37°C shaking incubator and shake at 300 RPM for 1 hour.

steps.title: Select and Verify Clones
steps.instruction: Plate the transformed cells and verify the resulting plasmids.

substeps.instruction: Plate 100 uL on Tryptone-Yeast extract + Spectinomycin + Sucrose agar plates and grow overnight at 37°C.
Pick colonies into LB + Spectinomycin and grow overnight at 37°C with shaking.
Perform miniprep and QC the plasmid (whole plasmid Nanopore sequencing is highly recommended).
